title.narrative: United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement and global value chains ¿ impact for EU companies

description.narrative: The objective of this project is to support the development of EU trade policy, with an analysis of the evolution of supply chains in North America, following the conclusion and implementation of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), as well as relevant related legislative developments, notably the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) in the United States. Specifically, the examination would contribute to improving the implementation of EU trade agreements with Canada and Mexico, as well as improve the knowledge base for future possible trade initiatives with the US and North America more generally. It will focus on sectors of main EU interest and most prominent EU FDI in North America such as: automotive, machinery, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, aerospace and defence.

title.narrative: Improve knowledge of the structure of relevant supply chains in North America and the main drivers of EU investments in North America in the sectors subject to the study. For this purpose, identify patterns and actors of downstream and upstream suppliers per sectors identified and describe the evolution of relevant EU exports/imports and investments from/to North America until now.Provide quantitative assessments on how European trade and investment flows in the identified sectors could be affected following relevant North American FTA changes as well as supply chainrelated domestic policy measures as indicated above (in background and global objective).Identify low hanging fruit that could provide and/or improve access to North American markets, which would in turn increase trade, investment, and business opportunities for European companies.Crosscutting objectives to be considered when addressing specific objectives: environment and climate change, rightbased approach, gender equality, disadvantaged groups and persons with disabilities and indigenous peoples.

A factual picture of upstream and downstream industries of supply chains per sector, key subsector, and its main drivers, e.g., FTAs, taxation, labor cost, logistics cost, energy cost, regulatory harmonization and/or compliance, environmental compliance costs, status of special economic zones and most importantly by geographical origin of intermediate sourcing. title.narrative: Output 2 The selected contractor will produce infographics for each sector studied, and for each geographical area (by country but also for individual States or Provinces of the U.S., Canada, and Mexico). For each sector, in each of the three countries a detailed infographic fiche, which would inter alia include overall number of companies participating in the various stages of the value chain (VC) of the sector, number of EU companies in the VC, outputs (whether end product or intermediate), location/s of production, logistic and other services. The infographics shall include trade links within companies in the same VC both in the domestic market, between the three countries, and with EU and rest of the world (measured in value), number of persons employed directly and indirectly in related sectors, and value of output and turnover.

Given the economic importance of the US market, the study will in particular examine relevant economic and regulatory characteristics in the US (around 50% of the study), but sufficient analysis will also be devoted to the Canadian and Mexican market conditions and developments (around 25% each).
